column1: # fail-open-sites.tsv — the disposition of every site the `pipeline` leg of
# anchor      A distinctive substring of the site's LINE. Text, never a line number: a
#             `file:line` key would red on every unrelated edit above it, and a guard that
#             cries wolf gets baselined away. The anchor must still appear in the file
#             (absence is ANCHOR DRIFT = red) and, for anything but `converted`, must still
#             cover a live enumerated site (a row that outlived its site is also red).
# why         What makes this disposition true. Not "looks fine" — name the mechanism.
# THE COUNT IS NOT THE CONTRACT. Three independent measurements of "the sites" disagreed
# (17 / 18 / 26) purely on scoping, so a completeness claim against a number is
# unfalsifiable. The guard's `--list` output is the denominator, and this file must cover
# it exactly — that pair is the contract, and neither half can rot without the other saying so.
# `converted` rows anchor on the REPLACEMENT text, so they are the one kind that must NOT
# cover a live site. Reverting a conversion therefore reds twice: the anchor stops resolving
# (or starts covering a site again), and the restored `| grep -q` reappears unclassified.

column4: Fails CLOSED. The site is the condition of an `if !` whose body prints ::error:: and exits 1, so a dead probe stops the job rather than passing it.

A `git worktree list` that fails means this is not a working repo, in which case the else arm's `git worktree add` fails loudly on the next line. The wrong branch is taken; nothing silently proceeds on a false answer.
The immediate producer is a `grep -v` filter over a shell variable — no file to fail reading, and its exit 1 means "everything was filtered", a genuine negative.
`cut` over a herestring has no failure mode short of OOM, and `$rows` was already proven readable by the `|| exit 2` on its own assignment.
Selftest-internal. A dead producer inside a test harness reds the suite; it cannot mislead production.
